title: Tenant SLO contracting matrix and onboarding checklist
author: Samira Patel
body:
Overview

This page documents the canonical SLO-to-capacity contract matrix used when onboarding new tenants to Redwood’s inference platform, plus the operational onboarding checklist runbook. The goal is to provide a repeatable negotiation and verification process that ties customer-visible SLOs to concrete capacity commitments, error-budget policies, and telemetry gates.

Scope
- Applies to hosted and dedicated tenants being onboarded by Platform/Customer Success.
- Covers initial SLO definition, capacity reservation, error-budget policy, monitoring/alerting configuration, and acceptance tests.
- Not a replacement for legal terms. This is the operational contract used by SRE / Platform to translate commercial commitments into runbookable controls.

Key definitions
- Tenant: a customer account (org) on Redwood.
- SLO: objective measured from production telemetry (availability, p99 latency, and quality where applicable).
- Error budget: allowed breach budget for a rolling 30d window unless otherwise agreed.
- Reserved headroom: pre-provisioned capacity (GPU slots / token-headroom) held for a tenant for burst absorption.

1) SLO — Capacity contract matrix (example)

| SLO name | Metric source | Quantile / target | Error budget (30d) | Reserved headroom | Escalation tier | On-call SLA |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| API availability | platform/ingress.healthy_ratio | >= 99.95% | 0.05% | 0.5 x baseline qps | Tier 1 (P0) | 1 hour |
| Text gen p99 (200 tokens) | runtime/latency_p99{model=\"rwd-gpt-4b\"} | <= 250ms | N/A (latency SLO) | 0.25 x baseline qps | Tier 1 | 1 hour |
| Embedding 95th | runtime/embedding_p95 | <= 180ms | N/A | 0.2 x baseline qps | Tier 2 | 4 hours |
| Quality regression (eval set) | quality/eval_score{promptset=\"tenant-A\"} | >= 0.92 | automatic rollback on -0.03 | N/A | Tier 2 | 4 hours |

Notes: Reserved headroom is expressed as a proportion of baseline (steady-state) QPS agreed during commercial onboarding. Baseline QPS is measured during the shadowing phase (see checklist).

2) Contract negotiation rules (operational policy)
- Default SLO template: availability 99.95% (30d), p99 latency targets per workload class, and quality gates for model-driven features.
- If a customer requires stronger SLOs, Platform must: (a) capture incremental reserved capacity required, (b) route financial uplift to Sales/Finance, and (c) enter a capacity-commitment ticket.
- Where the customer cannot pay for headroom, negotiate a reduced availability tier and add automatic fallback policies (cheaper quantized model or lower context).

3) Onboarding checklist (step-by-step runbook)
Preconditions: signed TA/contract, tenant account created, billing verified. Owner: Platform Engineer + Customer Success.

1. Discovery sync (owner: Solutions Engineer)
   - Collect workload profile: baseline QPS, peak QPS, distribution (gen/embedding), typical prompt lengths, and 99/95 token lengths.
   - Identify critical routes (e.g., chat vs. background embeddings) and data-sensitivity requirements.
2. Baseline shadowing (owner: Platform)
   - Deploy tenant in shadow mode for 72 hours. Capture: runtime service-level metrics, peak/median sequence lengths, and KV/cache hit distribution.
   - Prometheus query to capture baseline QPS: 
     sum(rate(http_requests_total{tenant_id=\"TENANT_X\"}[5m]))
   - Record steady-state QPS = 95th percentile of 5m-aggregated QPS from shadow window.
3. Populate contract matrix (owner: SRE)
   - Fill the matrix above with measured baseline and proposed reserved headroom. Save to the tenant record: /tenants/TENANT_X/contract-matrix.
4. Capacity reservation (owner: Capacity Manager)
   - If reserved headroom > 0, create a capacity allocation ticket and mark required GPU type, memory, and quantization profile. Example allocation: 2x A100-80GB equivalent for steady-state 150 qps embedding workload.
   - Set autoscaler min = reserved headroom floor, max = negotiated burst ceiling.
5. Monitoring & alerting (owner: Observability)
   - Create per-tenant dashboards and alerts wired to SLOs. Example alert: \"tenant-TENANT_X-p99-latency\" fires when p99 > target for 10m and consumes > 10% of error budget.
   - Example PromQL for p99 latency: histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(request_duration_seconds_bucket{tenant_id=\"TENANT_X\"}[5m])) by (le))
6. Error-budget policy config (owner: SRE)
   - Configure the error-budget engine with: window=30d, burn_rate_alert=4x (auto throttle), emergency_throttle_threshold=0.9 of headroom.
   - Set automated responses: if burn_rate > 8x for 1h -> open incident, if burn_rate > 4x for 6h -> throttle lower-priority routes.
7. Acceptance testing (owner: SRE + QA)
   - Run synthetic traffic at 1.2x baseline for 1 hour, verify SLOs hold and reserved headroom absorbs 100% of burst.
   - Run quality regression harness against tenant prompt-set (must pass configured quality gates).
8. Cutover and handoff (owner: Customer Success)
   - Move tenant traffic to production route with gradual ramp (10% -> 50% -> 100%) over 4 hours, monitor SLOs and error budget consumption.
   - Post-cutover 48h checkpoint: confirm metrics and sign-off.

4) Error-budget governance and automated controls
- Error-budget levels: green (>75% remaining), yellow (25–75%), red (<25%).
- Automated actions by level:
  - Yellow: notify tenant SRE contact and enable caching optimizations (prefix caching) and increased batching windows for non-latency-critical routes.
  - Red: start priority throttling (non-critical routes), enable model fallback to a cheaper variant, and, if configured, pause low-priority background jobs.
- Burn rate policies (examples):
  - If burn_rate > 4 for 6h -> SRE-runbook business-review and throttle non-critical traffic.
  - If burn_rate > 8 for 1h -> trigger P0 playbook and possible emergency capacity allocation.

5) Capacity proof & preflight (acceptance tests)
- Synthetic load harness steps:
  1) Replay 1x baseline (30m) to verify steady-state.
  2) Apply 1.5x burst (15m) to validate headroom absorption.
  3) Apply 2.0x extreme burst (5m) to observe graceful degradation behaviour.
- Required checks before production cutover:
  - Dashboard exam: no sustained alerts for 15m.
  - Error-budget status: must be green or yellow, not red.
  - Quality gate: pass.

6) Incident handling & post-incident requirements (tenant-specific)
- If tenant breaches SLOs beyond configured error-budget, follow standard incident process but include contract-specific attachments: the tenant contract matrix, reserved headroom allocation ticket, and the shadowing baseline report.
- Post-incident deliverables (owner: SRE):
  - For severity P0: 72-hour incident evidence packet and 10-day remediation plan.
  - For P1 with contract exposure: include capacity adjustment proposal and financial impact estimate.

7) Operational tooling integrations (how we implement controls)
- Capacity orchestration: Capacity Orchestrator service (capacity-orch) — create allocation via API:
  curl -X POST https://capacity-orch.internal/api/v1/allocations 
    -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN' 
    -d '{"tenant":"TENANT_X","gpu_type":"A100-80","reserved_slots":2,"min_replicas":2}'
- Error-budget engine: eb-engine — configure per-tenant policy with CLI:
  ebctl set-policy --tenant TENANT_X --window 30d --burn-alert 4 --emergency-throttle 0.9
- Monitoring: dashboards stored in grafana/dashboards/tenants/TENANT_X.json; alerts via alertmanager with route tenant-TENANT_X.

8) Roles & responsibilities (short)
- Platform: owns onboarding execution and capacity reservation tickets.
- SRE: owns contract matrix validation, error-budget policy, and acceptance tests.
- Observability: dashboards and alerting.
- Customer Success: coordinates cutover and sign-off.
- Sales/Finance: negotiates capacity uplift and pricing tied to reserved headroom.

9) Audit & review cadence
- Quarterly contract review between Platform, SRE, and Customer Success for high-value tenants. Items reviewed: baseline drift, error-budget consumption trends, model quality regressions, and recommended capacity adjustments.
- Annual capacity re-certification for on-prem/dedicated tenants (hardware footprint and quantization profile).

Appendix A — Example PromQL queries
- Baseline QPS (5m rate): sum(rate(http_requests_total{tenant_id=\"TENANT_X\"}[5m]))
- p99 latency: histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(request_duration_seconds_bucket{tenant_id=\"TENANT_X\"}[5m])) by (le))
- 30d availability (synthetic canary):
  sum_over_time(canary_success_total{tenant_id=\"TENANT_X\"}[30d:1d]) / sum_over_time(canary_total{tenant_id=\"TENANT_X\"}[30d:1d])

Appendix B — Example acceptance checklist (condensed)
- [ ] Shadowing window completed (72h)
- [ ] Contract matrix saved to tenant record
- [ ] Capacity reservation ticket created & approved
- [ ] Dashboards & alerts configured
- [ ] Error-budget engine policy enabled
- [ ] Synthetic acceptance tests passed
- [ ] Quality gate passed
- [ ] Cutover ramp completed and 48h checkpoint passed
